known_risks: all near-miss pairs share an LGA, so LGA agreement cannot help there; the cross-encoder carries it
the reviewer sees the engine's 'different' on every near-miss row
near_miss_construction: for each GRID3 facility in Edo, Kano and Ondo (salted order), the HFR facility in the same LGA with the closest name under character TF-IDF (cosine >= 0.35), not surfaced by today's engine run with it, kept only if arche.compare calls it different; 80 per state; records of the 2026-08-19 pack and pairs of the X1 pack excluded (data/scripts/build_near_miss_pack.py)
question: Do the X1 and X0 deciders keep false merges within bound when the test holds enough different pairs?

rule.deciders: unchanged: the X1 combiner refitted exactly as X1 fitted it (checked against X1's recorded weights) with its development thresholds; X0's cross-encoder with its recorded crosswalk thresholds
rule.error_bound: errors among auto-decided <= 3% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 10%
rule.false_merge_bound: different pairs auto-matched / all different pairs <= 2% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 5%
rule.informative: void unless the test holds at least 60 different pairs
rule.pass: informative, and every one of the 3 seeds meets fewer_held, error_bound and false_merge_bound
rule.population: the X1 pack's 272 labelled pairs together with the near-miss pack's pairs (data/review_packs/nigeria_facilities_nearmiss_2026-11-21, 240) marked same_entity or different; the near-miss labels are read once, after this file
rule.reference: match-everything is scored under the same rule; it must fail for the rule to mean anything
secondary: the X1 and near-miss parts reported separately

why: X1 passed on 264 same / 8 different, where match-everything also passed; that pack could not show false merges
